subject: FA7F518560E2EA0BDBF743A1577F0DDB
introduction: “I am weak, strengthen me in Thy Cause. I am poor, enrich me from the treasures of Thy Kingdom.” These prayers ask for help, and nearly always for help in order to do something: to serve, to teach, to bear what must be borne. They start from an inventory of what is lacking. “Ask, and it shall be given you”, the psalms of help from the hills and out of the depths, and Paul’s “my strength is made perfect in weakness” are the same prayer in scripture. Poor Richard’s proverb is the objection.
questions: What do these prayers ask help for? How often is it for the comfort of the one praying?
Why begin a prayer by listing one’s weaknesses?
“God helps them that help themselves.” Is that a different religion from these prayers, or the other half of the same one?

outside.why: A group scattered and dispersed, yet Thine. Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity!
Illumine my face with the radiance of Thy bounty. The Lord make his face shine upon thee, and be gracious unto thee.
The weak one seeking the dawning-place of Thy strength. He giveth power to the faint; and to them that have no might he increaseth strength.
Open the way for this helpless one. Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you.
Grant this feeble servant a shelter beneath Thy shade. Under his wings shalt thou trust.
I am weak, strengthen me; poor, enrich me. My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness.
Poor Richard: God helps them that help themselves. These prayers begin by confessing that the one praying cannot help himself. Which is the truer account of how help comes?
Exalt the humiliation of Thy servants. He hath put down the mighty from their seats, and exalted them of low degree.
This weak one has raised his hands. I will lift up mine eyes unto the hills, from whence cometh my help.
O Thou in Whose grasp lie the reins of the seen and unseen. Let us come boldly unto the throne of grace, that we may find grace to help in time of need.
Thy righteous servants beneath the claws of the wicked. Out of the depths have I cried unto thee, O Lord. Lord, hear my voice.
Aid him and assist him in all affairs. I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me.

shortfall: Sixty further prayers ask assistance in the same terms for other persons; companions were set to the first eleven readings.
